outcome: Heterogeneous changes in placental cell types (e.g., trophoblast subtypes, immune cell subtypes)
Proportion of cytotrophoblast (CTB) and extravillous trophoblast (EVT) cells
Gene expression and enrichment in trophoblast cells
Involvement of cellular pathways (immune, nutrient transfer, hormone, oxidative stress)
cohort: The study participants included pregnant women whose placental tissue was collected from cesarean sections, consisting of 5 patients with Preeclampsia, 5 with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus, and 5 healthy controls.
finding: The human placenta is a dynamic, heterogeneous organ, and trophoblast cells in Preeclampsia and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus exhibit involvement in immune, nutrient transfer, hormone, and oxidative stress pathways, with T cells and macrophages playing an immune defense role.
cross-section timing: At the time of birth (placental tissue isolated from cesarean section)
